data.name: Wreck Sighted
data.description: The Ghost Ship has come down on the coast. A salvager on the shore has watched everyone who went aboard, and remembers who came back.
data.successDescription: You have your first chart. The Battle Arena takes it, the Information Board has this weekend's page, and the Wreck has more.

objectives.description:
The Ghost Ship hung over this coast longer than anyone's grandmother could remember. Three nights ago she came down.

A salvager sits at a driftwood fire below the wreck, mending a net. She does not look up. "Another one come to pick her bones. Sit, then. She's had better than you."

She lies on her side, and her crew still stand their posts on the tilted deck. Not ghosts. Worse: they remember their orders.

"Nobody goes aboard alone and comes back. Go in threes. The ones who come back bring coin, stores and paper. Charts, wet ones, drawn by the crew themselves."

nextObjectiveId.text: Why would the dead draw maps?

objectives.description:
"Each chart is the way into one corner of her, and she doesn't hold still, so it's good once. Folk run them alone, out of the Battle Arena, and what you carry in is all you get.

The low-tide charts and the rosters take you to the lower decks. Down there are the crew's own charts: what they buried, the works, the archive, the helm. And those lead to the places the crew sealed shut."

"Some come back from the deep with a lantern that won't go out. It points at the mountain, at Crownhold, the castle she sailed from. Someone still sits its throne and still gives orders.

Others come back with a ledger page or a stores list, and go looking for holds no chart shows. They come back heavy, or not at all."

nextObjectiveId.text: You've watched a lot of them come back

objectives.description:
"Four of them brought me shards. One off the wreck, one from the castle, one from the deep decks, one from the sealed stores. Different hands, same glass. Lay them side by side and they ring.

Under Crownhold the stair stops where the rock does. I've stood at the bottom. Something beneath it listens back."

"Small. And what you can't use, trade. Every chart and every shard has a buyer, so no road's ever closed for good.

I keep their watch log, too. It washes up a page at a time. I dry one each weekend and pin it on the Information Board: one watch's orders. Lately the name at the top isn't one of theirs."
She pulls a Tide Chart from inside her coat, salt-stiff and still damp at one corner. "Low tide opens her lower hull. Don't sit on it. She's already changing shape."
